question: Should OpenClaw intentionally use layered yielded-run vocabulary—`paused` for persisted session rows and `deferred` for task/cron outcomes—or standardize these public surfaces on one term?
rationale: The code defect is mechanically repairable, but the status name becomes a compatibility-sensitive persisted/API contract shared by core, plugins, tools, and UI.

options.title: Keep layered vocabulary
options.body: Use `paused` for session state and `deferred` for task or cron outcomes, matching the distinct lifecycle layers in the two PRs.

options.title: Standardize one term
options.body: Rename one or both public states and update persistence, APIs, UI, docs, and upgrade proof together before merge.

recommendation.title: Keep layered vocabulary
recommendation.body: Use `paused` for session state and `deferred` for task or cron outcomes, matching the distinct lifecycle layers in the two PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history owns both the recovery and chat reconciliation surfaces that define the permanent lifecycle contract.
